name: Jedaiah
overview: Jedaiah was a male Levite who served as the second-chosen priest among the twenty-four priestly courses. He belonged to the line of Ithamar, one of the two sons of Aaron appointed to priestly duties. His role signifies a specific and honored position within the Levitical priesthood as organized in ancient Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Jedaiah means 'YHWH has favored' or 'YHWH knows,' reflecting a personal connection to the Lord. This proper name emphasizes divine favor or knowledge, highlighting the spiritual significance embedded in his identity.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Jedaiah as a descendant of Ithamar, linking him to a particular branch of the Levitical priestly family. Beyond this lineage, no additional family relationships are recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Jedaiah's importance lies in his appointment as the second-chosen priest within the twenty-four divisions established for temple service, underscoring the organized and divinely guided structure of Israel's worship. His descent from Ithamar highlights the continuation of priestly duties through specific family lines, reflecting God's orderly provision for worship in Israel.
